scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I'm a 24-year-old male who's been working at Walmart for about a month. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which includes lifting heavy boxes. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s, who seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. She approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me instead of helping. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin that's about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I told her I was happy to help if she was having trouble, but I wasn't going to lift all her heavy boxes while she watched. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team talked to me and said that the next time someone asks for help, I should help them because that's part of being a team. I explained what happened, making sure to clarify the situation in case she exaggerated. I also mentioned that both of us are paid to do the same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I added that I'm not the designated heavy lifter and suggested discussing it further with HR if needed. Then I stormed off feeling annoyed. So, was I the asshole here? It seems like it's two against one, with the co-worker and the head guy against me. But I feel like I was just trying to set boundaries and not take on all her work. Let me think about this from different angles. On one hand, teamwork is important, and helping out a co-worker can make the work environment better. But on the other hand, I don't want to be taken advantage of or end up doing all the heavy lifting while she stands by. It's also possible that she felt uncomfortable asking for help or didn't know how to properly ask for assistance. Maybe I should have communicated differently. Instead of refusing outright, I could have asked her how I could assist her in lifting the box together. That way, it's a team effort, and I'm not doing all the work alone. Also, when the head guy approached me, I could have listened more and tried to understand his perspective before getting defensive. I also wonder if there's a gender dynamic at play here. As a male, I might feel more pressure to help, but it's important to set boundaries to avoid burnout. However, it's also crucial to be respectful and supportive of my co-workers, regardless of gender. In the end, I think the key is to find a balance between being a team player and maintaining fair expectations. Communication is essential, and perhaps I could have approached the situation with more empathy and willingness to collaborate rather than setting up a confrontation. So, was I the asshole? I think there's room for improvement in how I handled the situation, but I also feel that the expectations from the co-worker and the head guy might have been unrealistic. It's a tricky situation, and I can see both sides of the argument.
